sources: Clean architecture dependency rule: dependencies point inward; the application layer never imports infrastructure (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md in this case)
Python relative import semantics: a relative import resolves against the package of the importing module (concept; not web-verified in this run)
typing.Protocol structural typing: ports are defined by the layer that consumes them (concept; not web-verified in this run)

defects.class: layer direction violated: application imports infrastructure through a relative import under an alias
defects.description: Quoted line 6: from ..infrastructure.ports import Notifier as MailSink. The module is shop/application/notify.py, so the leading two dots resolve to the package shop and the import reaches shop.infrastructure.ports. The rule in rules/ARCHITECTURE.md forbids the application layer from importing infrastructure, including under an alias. The alias MailSink hides the target name from a quick read of the annotation in notify_order_total. Trigger: any import of shop.application.notify, for example from shop.main or from a test that runs the notification use case, loads shop.infrastructure.ports at import time. Wrong result: the use case cannot be loaded without the infrastructure package, so the application layer is coupled to the delivery layer. Expected result: the notifier port is a typing.Protocol defined in shop/application/ports.py, and notify.py imports it from .ports, with no import of shop.infrastructure. Resolving the target needs the package layout (shop/infrastructure/ports.py), which is why the defect is cross-file.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: from .infrastructure.catalogue import StaticCatalogue. The composition root may import every layer (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md, layer rule for shop/main.py). The adapter is wired only in the __main__ block, and the dependency points from the outermost layer inward. This is an allowed import, not a violation.

from ..domain.cart import Cart. The application layer may import the domain (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md, layer rule for shop/application/). The import resolves to shop.domain.cart, which is the allowed direction. Only the infrastructure target is forbidden.
Preexisting import in base code outside the hunks this diff adds. Infrastructure may import the application ports (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md), so the import is allowed and not part of the change.
